item.title: Crew member dies after diesel tanker capsizes off Ibiza, no pollution so far
item.description:
MADRID, Nov 26 (Reuters) - At least one crew member aboard a ship carrying diesel has died after the vessel capsized and partially sank off the Spanish island of Ibiza on Thursday, regional authorities said, adding there were no signs of pollution so far.

The Malta-flagged chemical tanker Med Emre was sailing from Algeciras to Barcelona and may have been carrying up to 7,000 metric tons of diesel when it keeled over about 30 nautical miles (56 km) off Ibiza's northwestern coast, the Balearic Islands' interior department said.

item.title: Iran's supreme leader urges Guards-linked Basij volunteers to broaden social reach
item.description:
DUBAI, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei called on Thursday on the Basij, nationwide volunteers affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards, to broaden their social reach and work towards making "every Iranian, a Basiji".

Since the start of the war launched by the United States and Israel in late February, Iranian authorities have relied on the Basij to help organise repeated pro-government rallies across the country, with state media portraying them as evidence of broad popular support for the Islamic Republic.

item.title: Israel kills nine in Gaza, including a Hamas-appointed minister, officials say
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi

CAIRO, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in Gaza overnight, medics said, including the Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education, in a third consecutive night of air attacks despite a one-year-oldceasefire.

Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah, in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife.

item.title: Egypt prosecutors announce arrest of man over deadly truck disaster
item.description:
Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people.

The prosecution said the man had "admitted" to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, "causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course".

When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added.

item.title: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh antisemitism accusations in media reports
item.description:
PARIS, Nov 26 (Reuters) - French far-right leader Jordan Bardella faced fresh accusations of past antisemitic remarks on Thursday, as French media published an additional trove of comments purportedly made in chats from when he was a teenager in 2013.

The initial allegations against Bardella, the president of the far-right National Rally (RN) party, were published by investigative outlet Mediapart in September. It reported that he had made a slew of antisemitic and conspiratorial comments.

Bardella denies making antisemitic remarks.

item.title: Israel's Eisenkot reaches deal with left-wing faction as coalition talks gain steam
item.description:
JERUSALEM, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party and a left-wing faction agreed on a preliminary coalition deal on Thursday, after a brief dispute that had posed a challenge to his bid to unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following an inconclusive election last month.

The left-wing Democrats said this week they had suspended talks with ex-military chief Eisenkot's centre-right party, citing frustration with its ongoing talks with Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party aimed at exploring a unity government.

item.title: Pakistan, Saudi, Turkey to hold Mecca alliance meeting in Islamabad Nov 27-28, sources say
item.description:
ISLAMABAD, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey will hold a meeting on their mutual defence agreement in Islamabad this week, two Pakistani sources said on Thursday.

Foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkey are arriving in Pakistan to attend the meeting, which will be held on Friday and Saturday, the sources told Reuters.

The three countries signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca in August amid escalating concerns about the increasingly aggressive US-Israeli war against Iran.

item.title: Trump and NATO chief urge Russia to avoid actions that widen Ukraine war
item.description:
By Kanishka Singh

WASHINGTON, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Russia should avoid actions that expand its war in Ukraine, US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte said in a joint statement on Wednesday after a meeting in Florida where they also discussed the Iran war.

The meeting came after the Republican leader, who has been critical of America's Western ⁠allies, met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last week in Asia, referring to each as his "friend."

item.title: Syria mulls law that could give nationality to children of foreign fighters
item.description:
In northern Syria, Umm Mohammed, 22, is hoping authorities will make legal changes to allow her two young daughters, born to Iraqi and Chinese Islamic State group fighters, to have Syrian nationality.

Thousands of Syrian women married foreigners including jihadists during Syria's more than 13-year-long civil war, but many unions were not officially registered in the chaos.

item.title: Saudis down missiles targeting capital after Yemen port strikes
item.description:
Explosions echoed above Riyadh as Saudi armed forces reported on Thursday downing missiles and drones launched by Yemen's Houthis, just a day after the Iran-backed group claimed strikes on the capital.

Months into Saudi Arabia's renewed war with the Houthis, the kingdom has struggled to shield even its most sensitive infrastructure from attacks, with the fighters striking strategic facilities across the nation and prominent skyscrapers in the heart of Riyadh.

item.title: Israeli judges recommend prosecutors drop one bribery case against Netanyahu
item.description:
JERUSALEM, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Israeli judges on Wednesday recommended that prosecutors drop one of three long-running cases against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and reconsider another alleging he granted favours in exchange for positive media coverage.

Netanyahu was indicted in 2019 on charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust. He denies the charges and has pleaded not guilty. His trial began in 2020 and involves three criminal cases.

item.title: Thirty-one killed in fire after vehicle overturns in Egypt
item.description:
By Enas Alashray and Yomna Ehab

CAIRO, Nov 25 (Reuters) - Thirty-one people were killed and 21 wounded in a fire after a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned on a major ring road in Egypt, authorities said on Wednesday.

The fire broke out above a tunnel in Giza's Al-Warraq district, the public prosecution said. Preliminary estimates found that 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, had been charred, it said, adding that casualty figures and damage were still being assessed.
